profile.name: Mohammed Saleeq Kolleth
profile.headline: Doctoral Candidate & Robotics Researcher
profile.subheadline: Bridging verifiable cognitive deliberation with production-grade engineering for robust robotic systems.
profile.about: I am an engineer turned researcher currently pursuing my doctorate as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Candidate at Universität Bremen in the SECORO Group (CAVECORE Project). My background spans mechanical engineering at IIT Tirupati, commercial automotive CAE simulation at Jaguar Land Rover, an MSc in Robotics (with Distinction) at the University of Birmingham, and research associate work on context-aware deliberation (EU CONVINCE Project). My goal is bringing mathematical rigor, formal verification, and cutting-edge AI into industrial robotics.

bullets: Doctoral candidate in the CAVECORE EU doctoral network investigating safety guarantees in Human-Robot Collaboration (HRC).
Pioneering Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines for contextual hazard anticipation and verifiable runtime safety reasoning.
Collaborating with European research and industrial partners to bridge software engineering with cognitive robotics.

experience.organization: University of Birmingham — Intelligent Robotics Lab
bullets: Designed and implemented reinforcement learning–based manipulation strategies for robotic planning under uncertainty.
Built hierarchical deliberation pipelines integrating py_trees_ros (Behavior Trees), symbolic planners (PDDLStream), and trajectory controllers in ROS2.
Integrated real hardware: Universal Robots UR10e and Kinova Gen3 manipulator platforms.
Explored Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based planners for cognitive reasoning in Task and Motion Planning (TAMP).
Co-authoring a manuscript on plan refinement under uncertainty (target: IEEE RA-L).

experience.organization: Jaguar Land Rover (ODEC) subcontracted via TATA ELXSI

Developed CAD/CAE models and kinematic simulations for automotive and consumer product engineering.

projects.title: HAMCBS: Human-Aware Multi-Robot Motion Planner
projects.description: Multi-agent pathfinding framework integrating Conflict-Based Search (CBS) with Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Social Force Models to coordinate robot fleets in shared human-occupied environments.
highlights: Resolves multi-agent path conflicts while respecting pedestrian psychological comfort zones via social force potential fields.
Implemented in ROS2 with full Gazebo physics simulation and dynamic obstacle avoidance.
Scalable collision resolution benchmarked across varying human density levels.

projects.title: Variance-Based Particle Filter Localization
projects.description: An adaptive Monte-Carlo localization algorithm augmented with spatial variance estimation and DBSCAN clustering to solve the catastrophic 'kidnapped robot' problem.
highlights: Continuous statistical monitoring of particle cluster spread to instantly identify localization divergence.
Density-based spatial clustering (DBSCAN) isolates multimodal hypothesis clouds and rapidly recovers true robot pose.
Benchmarked on complex floorplans under extreme sensor dropout and random pose teleportation.

projects.title: RoboConvoy: Multi-Agent POMDP Transporter System
projects.description: Coordinated multi-agent autonomous robotic transport system collaboratively planning, navigating, and transporting sizable payloads across complex indoor environments under partial observability and spatial uncertainty.
highlights: Formulates collective transport as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) solved in continuous belief space via Point-Based Value Iteration (PBVI).
Multi-modal Particle Filter Localization (MCL) accelerated with C++ laser ray-tracing and DBSCAN spatial clustering for robust kidnap recovery.
Composite formation abstraction: agents enclose and secure the payload, transitioning dynamically to a single kinematic entity during transit.
Validated across high-fidelity 3D Gazebo and 2D Stage multi-robot simulation environments.

projects.title: CoppeliaSim UR10e Manipulation Framework
projects.description: Simulation framework and Python programmatic interface for the Universal Robots UR10e industrial manipulator in CoppeliaSim.
highlights: Provides modular Python API for forward/inverse kinematics, trajectory smoothing, and collision-free pick-and-place.
Integrates virtual depth cameras and force-torque sensors for closed-loop manipulation experiments.
Served as simulation prototyping environment for real robot deployment.

projects.title: Analytical Thermo-Mechanical WAAM Simulator
projects.description: Analytical solution and programmatic finite-element thermo-mechanical simulation for Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM) coupled with KUKA industrial robot paths.
highlights: Derived temperature distribution and residual stress equations for continuous multi-layer weld deposition.
Experimental validation conducted at Lincoln Electric with KUKA KR IONTEC arm using submerged arc (SAW) and MIG welding.
Implemented in Python with CoppeliaSim kinematic validation.

publications.title: Plan Refinement Under Uncertainty for Robotic Manipulation
publications.authors: M. S. Kolleth et al. (CONVINCE Project Consortium)
publications.venue: Manuscript in Preparation (Target: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters - RA-L)
publications.summary: Presents a hierarchical deliberation architecture combining behavior trees (py_trees_ros) with symbolic-geometric Task and Motion Planning (PDDLStream) to dynamically refine plans when perceptual and action uncertainties arise during manipulation.

publications.title: HAMCBS: Human-Aware Multi-Robot Motion Planner for Shared Workspaces
publications.venue: Master's Thesis with Distinction — University of Birmingham
publications.summary: Developed a two-level planner incorporating Social Force Models into CBS low-level search and MPC trajectory optimization to respect human personal space during multi-robot fleet coordination.

publications.title: A Robust Multi-Agent Transporter Robot System With Contextual Intelligence
publications.authors: Mohammed Saleeq Kolleth, Rahim Khan, Martin Muru, Mohammadali Moghimi, Alan Binu
publications.venue: Technical Report & Benchmark — Intelligent Robotics, University of Birmingham
publications.summary: Formulated a cooperative multi-robot payload transportation system under perceptual and environmental uncertainty using Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes solved via Point-Based Value Iteration (PBVI) with composite formation kinematic abstraction.

publications.title: Thermo-Mechanical Modelling for Robotic Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing (WAAM)
publications.authors: Mohammed Saleeq Kolleth (Supervised at J&M Lab, IIT Tirupati & Lincoln Electric)
publications.summary: Programmatic analytical solution for transient temperature distributions and residual stress profiles in additive manufacturing, validated on industrial KUKA robotic welding systems.
